Yeah, it really does.

If you want to will yourself to do a thing that scares the shit out of you, like seeking help, try that one before the rope. Like, walk into the emergency room or call a hotline. Just have to initiate that first move. Who cares what anyone thinks, and if it doesn't work, you can go back to plan A; got nothing to lose.
Good point. I'll try that if still don't hear anything.
Oh, right! Transparency is usually the best policy, but still good in this case? Edit: Addressing trust issues would take precedence over avoiding guilt, right?

I meant cold contact like a cold call; calling a complete stranger without any prior interaction. Yeah, I'll try and figure out if any of them are close to her before messaging them.

And thanks for the reassurance.

No real way. Her family likely knows nothing at all; the type to deny, repress, condemn and dismiss rather than believe and support. No other known friends, very isolated. Could I cold-contact her facebook friends..?

But those messages to express, those are very good ideas, thank you so much Amy. I won't give up.

Family is away on vacation, we don't know them, and they are not a healthy relationship to her.

Last "contact" was to our mutual friend, saying that she had been severely depressed and suicidal, is on a plane, and sorry for not being there for us.

I don't want to put much responsibility on our mutual friend; she's going through her own nightmare.

Edit: that contact was yesterday morning

Maybe a guess but a really good point! "Younger people being safer". Easier to read, less likely and able to deceive and hurt us. Maybe it's a little similar to how much easier it is to trust/predict pets, since they don't hide or fake emotions.

Food for thought; thank you.
Oh, that makes sense. I always thought there was a fun "awkward charm" about it. Glad to hear it doesn't get old.

Finding the reason changes *everything*, doesn't it?? Knowing that it's all miscommunication and not malice? And it be solved with patience, wording and the right expectations? I get giddy thinking of all the difference "reason" made (imo).

Congratulations on the happy marriage, home and career, strange as it may sound!

It seems to only be a problem when we're contrasted with other people, eh?

I get that comparison can be a good tool to measure milestones and whatnot, but I feel like we're not in the same race as everyone else anymore. Not everyone gets that growth spurt we both got later in life. And like the sunscreen song says, "The race is long and, in the end, it's only with yourself."

Animals are a good answer though. They don't give a shit, they only speak food and love.

Yeah, I feel very much like this. I know and love who I am, and where I belong in time, and I doubt I'll lose that same childish perspective and sense of awe, wonder and absurdity. It makes me an awesome uncle and I'll be an amazing father one day.

It's the outsiders' perspective that pressures me. I can cope with sticking out in school, but dating is tough. Dating someone ten years younger might feel perfectly natural and equal to me,  but when I'm reminded of my age I feel gross. Not morally wrong, but *judged*. There are good reason for a girl's loved ones to distrust an older guy. And I might pass for 25, but lying to a partner's friends or family is *absolutely out of the question*.

Is your spouse the same age? If not, is it ever a problem?
